A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRISM by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PRISM sequence-recovery, foldability, runtime, ablation, memory-growth, and diversity results across five benchmarks.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds orphan-protein evaluation, finetuning and refinement experiments, initializer analyses, and structural designability results.

M1.justification: Beyond the retained deterministic implementation, v2 introduces a trainable retrieval pathway that finetunes the joint encoder using a KL-regularized objective (Section 3.8 and Appendix E.2). It also adds inference-time iterative feedback of PRISM's generated sequences (Section 4.3.7). These change training and inference procedures; v1's implemented training optimized the structure encoder and decoder with fixed retrieval.

E1.justification: v2 adds the eleven-protein orphan benchmark, described as lacking detectable sequence homologs, to test novel-backbone generalization. This is a focused extension of evaluation coverage within inverse folding. The original five benchmarks and CATH-4.2 training coverage remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds scored comparisons against VFN-IF and VFN-IFE in the CATH-4.2 recovery/designability comparison (Appendix Table 17), using baseline results attributed to Mao et al. The original main-table comparator sets remain. SurfPro, SurfDesign, and BC-Design are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces ESMFold-based evaluation on CATH-4.2 and orphan proteins, including designability percentages defined by scTM > 0.5 and scRMSD < 2. It adds controlled comparisons of frozen versus finetuned encoders, single-pass versus iterative generation, and alternative initializers. These extend the evaluation design; the original splits and AlphaFold2 evaluations are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test encoder adaptation and iterative refinement (Table 9), dependence on the base estimator (Table 10), and sensitivity to initial prediction quality through AAR bins (Table 11). Orphan evaluation probes generalization without detectable homologs, and Appendix L adds threshold-based designability analysis. Existing retrieval-count, attention, depth, memory-growth, length, and diversity analyses remain.

E5.justification: The existing mean/median summaries, distribution plots, Figure 9 error bars, and 100 sampled sequences per backbone are retained. v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result entries for orphan proteins, CATH foldability/designability, finetuning, refinement, and initializer sensitivity. For example, the new finetuned, iterative PRISMaido variant reports CATH AAR 63.33%, while the retained original variant reports 60.43%; these are different configurations. Original benchmark scores and relocated foldability/ablation entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a factorized-posterior ELBO decomposition supporting a trainable retrieval prior. Section 2 also replaces the autoregressive chain-rule factorization with a product of backbone-conditioned residue probabilities, and Section 3.6 corrects attribution conditioning to include E. The existing ELBO, deterministic-reduction, Top-K convergence, and coverage results are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the principal claims: residue-level multimodal retrieval for inverse folding, a latent-variable formulation, state-of-the-art recovery and foldability, and low runtime overhead. The additional variants and experiments do not materially redefine the stated main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning resistance to memorization, independence from a particular initializer, and benefits of encoder adaptation and iterative feedback. It proposes possible compatibility with surface- and biochemistry-based generators and identifies further posterior learning/refinement as future work. Its orphan-protein claim of consistent improvement exceeds the mixed evidence in Table 6.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.3 reports the CPU, RAM, four 40-GB A100 GPUs, and 15.1-GB database storage requirement. Appendix B.4 discloses masking to prevent training-time self-retrieval. These improve implementation disclosure; v1's silence does not establish that the masking procedure changed. Detailed finetuning and iterative-refinement settings remain underspecified.

R1.justification: v2 extends related work to VFN-IF/VFN-IFE and surface- or biochemistry-based design through SurfPro, SurfDesign, and BC-Design, positioning the latter as an orthogonal direction. It also adds references supporting orphan evaluation, ESMFold, and designability protocols. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: detailed stochastic retrieval, the derived probabilistic model, and deterministic training derivations move from the main method section into Appendices D/E. Benchmark discussions are consolidated under Section 4.2, and the appendices are restructured. The abstract is rewritten, variant terminology is expanded, and conference headers and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1 with structural metrics and adds tables for orphan evaluation, finetuning/refinement, initializer comparisons, prediction-quality bins, and designability. Original foldability and attention/depth tables are split between the main text and appendices without losing their results. Figure 2 is relocated and its labeling revised; Figures 3–4 are restyled, while the other original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 better examines dependence on initialization through Tables 9–11, adds stronger CATH comparators and designability evidence, and improves hardware and self-retrieval documentation. These strengthen the paper beyond v1. The gains are qualified by underspecified new training/refinement procedures and overstated orphan conclusions: Table 6 reports ProteinMPNN-CMLM AAR of 29.27% versus 27.12% for PRISMmpnn despite the claim of consistent improvement. Overall, the evidence and transparency improve, but the remaining methodological and interpretive weaknesses limit the gain.
